docs.title: Welcome to TRACE
docs.text:
TRACE (Triggered Radiotherapy Adaptive Control Engine) is a dedicated software suite designed to control and verify dynamic anthropomorphic thorax phantoms used in 4D Radiotherapy (4DRT), motion management research, and image-guided radiation therapy (IGRT).

As described in Lustermans et al. (2024), TRACE interfaces with multi-axis motion hardware and triggering electronics to simulate realistic patient breathing motions and evaluate 4DCT and radiotherapy treatment delivery.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Analytical & Patient-Derived Motion Profiles:
    • Generate synthetic respiratory waveforms (sinusoidal, \(\cos^4\), custom analytical functions).
    • Import and process patient-derived respiratory curves from 4DCT/RPM clinical logs.
    • Scale, smooth, adjust baseline drift, and resample motion profiles.
  • Multi-Axis Trajectory Planning:
    • Full 6-DOF support (Translational: SI, AP, LR; Rotational: Roll, Pitch, Yaw).
    • Automated G-code generation optimized for Duet motion controllers.
  • Hardware Integration & Real-Time Control:
    • Direct communication with Duet 3D motion platform controllers.
    • Real-time axis homing, position tracking, and manual jogging.
  • Triggered Imaging & Verification:
    • Hardware synchronization with Geiger module for triggered imaging acquisition.
    • Live plotting and position error monitoring during motion execution.

docs.title: User Guide Overview
docs.text:
This User Guide provides end-to-end instructions for setting up, operating, and troubleshooting TRACE:

  1. Installation: Setting up the Python environment and launching TRACE.
  2. Hardware Setup: Connecting the Duet controller, phantom stage, and Geiger trigger module.
  3. Files & Project Management: Managing project directories and patient motion datasets.
  4. Motion Planning & G-code: Creating analytical waveforms, editing patient curves, and exporting G-code.
  5. Phantom Control & Execution: Homing, running motion trajectories, and triggering.
  6. Real-Time Status & Monitoring: Live verification, logging, and performance metrics.
  7. Troubleshooting & Safety: Resolving connection issues, limit switch stops, and safety protocols.

Download PDF Manual

When built with the with-pdf plugin, the complete documentation is available as a single downloadable PDF manual under exports/TRACE_User_Guide.pdf.

docs.title: Hardware Setup & Wiring
docs.text: This guide details the physical hardware setup for connecting the dynamic anthropomorphic thorax phantom, the motion platform controller, and the triggering hardware to TRACE.

docs.title: Hardware Architecture
docs.text:
The TRACE ecosystem consists of three main hardware components:

+-------------------+        Ethernet / USB       +---------------------------+
|                   | <-------------------------> |  Duet Motion Controller   |
|   Workstation     |                             |   (Stepper Axis Drivers)  |
|  Running TRACE    |                             +---------------------------+
|                   |                                           |
|                   |        RS-232 / USB                       v
|                   | <-------------------------> +---------------------------+
+-------------------+                             | Dynamic Thorax Phantom    |
                                                  | (SI, AP, LR & Rotational) |
                                                  +---------------------------+
                                                                |
                                                                v
                                                  +---------------------------+
                                                  | Geiger Triggering Module  |
                                                  |   (4DCT / Linac Sync)     |
                                                  +---------------------------+

docs.title: 1. Duet Motion Controller Setup
docs.text:
TRACE communicates with a Duet 3D motion controller via HTTP REST API or Direct Serial Interface.

  1. Network Cable: Connect an Ethernet cable from your workstation/switch to the Duet Ethernet port.
  2. IP Configuration: Ensure the IP address matches duet_ip in configuration.json (Default: 192.168.1.100).
  3. Axis Assignments:
    • Axis X: Superior-Inferior (SI) translation.
    • Axis Y: Anterior-Posterior (AP) translation.
    • Axis Z: Left-Right (LR) translation.
    • Axis U / V / W: Rotational axes (Roll, Pitch, Yaw).

Emergency Stop Button

Always test the hardware E-STOP button wired to the Duet controller before running automated motion sequences.

docs.title: 2. Geiger Triggering Module Setup
docs.text:
The Geiger module enables synchronized X-ray imaging / 4DCT triggering during specific phases of phantom motion.

  1. Serial Connection: Plug the USB-to-Serial adapter from the Geiger module into the workstation.
  2. Identify Port: Note the assigned COM port (Windows: COMx, Linux/macOS: /dev/ttyUSBx).
  3. Trigger Output: Connect the opto-isolated trigger output cable to the external trigger input of the imaging modality (Linac / CT scanner).

docs.title: 3. Power-On Checklist
docs.text:
Before launching TRACE:

  • [ ] Verify 24V power supply connected to Duet controller.
  • [ ] Confirm phantom motion stage is free from physical obstacles.
  • [ ] Confirm Geiger module LED power indicator is green.
  • [ ] Ping Duet IP (ping 192.168.1.100) from command prompt.

docs.title: Installation & Software Setup
docs.text: This page guides you through installing the required dependencies and launching the TRACE Graphical User Interface (GUI).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing TRACE, ensure you have installed:

  • Python 3.10 or later (Conda or Miniconda environment recommended).
  • Git (for repository cloning).

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the TRACE repository using Git or your preferred Git client (e.g., SourceTree, GitHub Desktop):

git clone https://github.com/YourUsername/TRACE.git
cd TRACE

docs.title: Step 2: Create Conda Environment
docs.text:
TRACE provides an environment.yml file containing all required packages (PyQt / DearPyGui, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, PySerial, etc.).

Create and activate the environment:

conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate trace-env

Alternatively, if installing dependencies manually via pip:

pip install numpy scipy matplotlib pyqt5 pyserial requests

docs.title: Configuration (configuration.json)
docs.text:
Check configuration.json in the root directory to verify hardware settings (IP address of Duet controller, default COM ports for Geiger module, default baud rates):

{
  "duet_ip": "192.168.1.100",
  "geiger_port": "COM3",
  "baud_rate": 115250,
  "default_output_dir": "./output"
}

docs.title: Launching TRACE
docs.text:
To launch the graphical user interface, run Launch_ImGUI.py:

python Launch_ImGUI.py

First Launch Verification

Upon successful launch, the TRACE interface window will open, displaying the navigation tabs (Files, Planning, Control, Status) and initializing the communication threads in the background.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Safety Guide
docs.text: This guide covers common operational issues, hardware error messages, recovery procedures, and safety protocols when running TRACE with the dynamic phantom.

docs.title: 1. "Duet Controller Disconnected / Timeout"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Red status indicator, commands fail to send.

Solutions: - Verify Ethernet cable connection between workstation and Duet. - Test network connectivity: 

ping 192.168.1.100
- Open browser and navigate to http://192.168.1.100 to confirm Duet Web Control (DWC) is responding. - Verify IP address matches duet_ip in configuration.json.

docs.title: 2. "Geiger Serial Port COMx Not Found"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Cannot toggle trigger synchronization or test pulses.

Solutions: - Unplug USB-to-Serial cable and re-insert. - Open Device Manager (Windows) or run ls /dev/tty* (Linux) to check assigned port number. - Update geiger_port in configuration.json and restart TRACE.

docs.title: 3. "Axis Hit Limit Switch / Endstop Triggered"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Emergency stop activated, movement freezes mid-trajectory.

Solutions: 1. Check physical platform position for mechanical obstruction or extreme travel. 2. Click Reset Controller Alarm. 3. Use manual jog controls in reverse direction at low speed (\(0.1\,\text{mm}\)) to backed off switch. 4. Verify motion trajectory limits in Planning Tab before re-running.

docs.title: 4. "Buffer Underrun / Stuttering Motion"
docs.text:
Symptoms: Phantom movement stutters or pauses intermittently.

Solutions: - Reduce point density / increase step interval in Planning Tab during G-code generation. - Close CPU-intensive background applications. - Switch connection mode from Serial to Ethernet REST API for higher throughput.

docs.title: Safety Protocols
docs.text:
Laboratory Safety Guidelines

  • Never place hands or tools inside the phantom motion stage while power is applied.
  • Keep the hardware Emergency Stop button within easy reach during all automated trajectory runs.
  • Inspect motor belts and mechanical fasteners weekly for wear or tension loss.

docs.title: Chapter 1: Files & Project Management
docs.text: The Files Tab in TRACE (tab_files.py) is the entry point for importing raw patient motion data, managing analytical waveform presets, and selecting output directories for generated G-code files.

docs.title: Files Tab Overview
docs.text:
When you open the Files tab, you will find:

  • Project Directory Selector: Choose where motion data and G-code outputs are saved.
  • Raw Data Import Panel: Load CSV, TSV, DICOM, or log files containing respiratory motion traces.
  • Preset Library: Select pre-defined standard motion templates (e.g., standard sinusoidal breathing, irregular breathing, high-frequency motion).

docs.title: 1. Importing Patient Respiratory Curves
docs.text: TRACE supports importing patient-derived motion profiles captured by clinical motion tracking systems (such as RPM, Anzai, or Varian RGSC).

docs.title: Supported File Formats
docs.text: Format Extensions Description CSV / TSV .csv, .tsv, .txt Columnar data containing time vs displacement columns. RPM Logs .vms, .txt Varian Real-Time Position Management log files. G-code .gcode, .g Pre-compiled Duet G-code trajectory files.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Import Procedure
docs.text:
1. Click Browse File under the Import Motion Data panel.
  2. Select your raw motion file.
  3. Specify the time column index and motion axis column index.
  4. Click Parse File. TRACE will render a preview plot of the imported waveform.

docs.title: 2. Managing Project Directory & Outputs
docs.text:
Outputs generated by TRACE (such as compiled .gcode files and trajectory logs) are stored in the selected Project Directory.

  • Set Default Directory: Use Select Directory to choose your target folder.
  • File Naming Convention: 
    <project_name>_<axis>_<waveform_type>.gcode
    Example: planned_motion_platform_SI_sin.gcode

Organizing Patient Datasets

We recommend creating a separate subfolder for each patient or phantom study inside your project directory to keep G-code and verification logs organized.

docs.title: Chapter 2: Motion Planning & G-code Export
docs.text: The Planning Tab (tab_planning.py & fcn_plan) is where motion profiles are designed, edited, mathematically transformed, and compiled into controller-ready G-code.

docs.title: 1. Creating Analytical Waveforms
docs.text: TRACE allows you to generate synthetic mathematical motion curves to simulate standard breathing patterns or mechanical test signals.

docs.title: Available Analytical Waveform Types
docs.text:
1. Sinusoidal Curve: $\(z(t) = A \cdot \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{T} t + \phi\right) + z_0\)$
  2. \(A\): Amplitude (mm)
  3. \(T\): Breathing period (seconds)
  4. \(\phi\): Phase offset (rad)

  5. \(z_0\): Baseline offset (mm)

  6. Modified \(\cos^4\) Breathing Curve: Simulates realistic asymmetry between inspiration and expiration phases: $\(z(t) = A \cdot \cos^4\left(\frac{\pi}{T} t\right) + z_0\)$

  7. Trapezoidal / Step Motion: Used for step response tests and static phantom offset calibrations.

docs.title: 2. Editing Patient-Derived Motion Curves
docs.text:
Raw clinical respiratory traces often contain baseline drift, high-frequency noise, or cardiac artifacts. TRACE provides interactive tools in fcn_edit.py to refine these profiles:

  • Baseline Correction: Removes gradual baseline elevation drift over time.
  • Amplitude Scaling: Rescales motion to match specific phantom limits (e.g., max 30 mm SI displacement).
  • Smoothing / Filtering: Applies Savitzky-Golay or low-pass Butterworth filtering to eliminate signal noise.
  • Resampling: Interpolates motion data to match the Duet motor update frequency (typically 50 Hz or 100 Hz).

docs.title: 3. Multi-Axis Preview
docs.text:
Before exporting G-code, preview the 6-DOF motion components in the interactive plot panel:

  • SI Axis (Z-motion): Primary Superior-Inferior displacement.
  • AP Axis (Y-motion): Anterior-Posterior displacement.
  • LR Axis (X-motion): Left-Right displacement.
  • Rotational Axes (Roll, Pitch, Yaw): Rotational tilting.

docs.title: 4. Exporting G-Code for Duet Controller
docs.text:
Once you are satisfied with the trajectory:

  1. Select target motor acceleration and velocity limits.
  2. Click Generate G-Code (fcn_gcode.py).
  3. TRACE compiles linear/curved segment commands: 
    G90 ; Absolute positioning mode
G1 X12.4 Y2.1 Z-5.0 F1200 ; Linear move with feedrate 1200 mm/min
G1 X12.8 Y2.3 Z-4.8 F1250
  4. Click Save G-Code to store the .gcode file into your project output directory.

docs.title: Chapter 3: Phantom Control & Execution
docs.text: The Control Tab (tab_control.py & fcn_control.py) provides direct control over the dynamic thorax phantom hardware, motor initialization, manual jogging, G-code execution, and trigger synchronization.

docs.title: 1. Connecting to Hardware
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Control tab.
  2. Select connection mode: Ethernet (REST API) or Serial (COM).
  3. Click Connect Controller.
  4. Check connection status indicator:
    • 🟢 Connected: IP / COM port open and responding.
    • 🔴 Disconnected: Verify wiring or IP settings in configuration.json.

docs.title: 2. Homing & Zeroing Axes
docs.text:
Before executing any motion trajectory, the physical platform MUST be homed to establish mechanical zero reference points.

  1. Ensure the platform path is clear.
  2. Click Home All Axes (\(G28\)).
  3. Wait for all axis status indicators to turn green.
  4. Verify position readout shows (0.00, 0.00, 0.00).

Axis Safety Limits

Never attempt to run G-code without homing first. Running motion profiles from un-homed positions can cause mechanical collision against endstops.

docs.title: 3. Manual Jogging
docs.text:
Use the manual jog panel to fine-tune phantom position or perform pre-experiment align checks:

  • Step Sizes: \(0.1\,\text{mm}, 1.0\,\text{mm}, 5.0\,\text{mm}, 10.0\,\text{mm}\).
  • Directions: \(\pm X, \pm Y, \pm Z, \pm \text{Roll}, \pm \text{Pitch}, \pm \text{Yaw}\).
  • Feedrate Control: Adjustable speed slider (\(10 - 3000\,\text{mm/min}\)).

docs.title: 4. Running Motion Trajectories
docs.text:
To execute a planned G-code motion file:

  1. Click Select G-Code File and pick your compiled trajectory.
  2. Select execution mode:
    • Single Cycle: Plays motion sequence once and returns to home.
    • Continuous Loop: Repeats motion sequence until manually stopped.
  3. Click Start Motion.
  4. Use Pause Motion (\(M600\)) or Emergency Stop (\(M112\)) at any time to halt movement.

docs.title: 5. Geiger Triggering Configuration
docs.text:
To enable imaging/gating triggers during specific phases of the trajectory:

  1. Toggle Enable Geiger Trigger Sync.
  2. Set Phase Trigger Point (e.g., peak inspiration at \(90^\circ\) or end expiration at \(270^\circ\)).
  3. Set Pulse Duration (e.g., \(50\,\text{ms}\)).
  4. Click Test Trigger Signal to verify optocoupler pulse output on the Geiger hardware module.

docs.title: Chapter 4: Real-Time Status & Monitoring
docs.text: The Status Tab (tab_status.py, fcn_duet.py, fcn_plotting.py) monitors motion execution in real time, displays live feedback plots, and logs trigger events for post-experiment validation.

docs.title: 1. Live Motion Tracking Plots
docs.text:
During motion execution, TRACE renders real-time multi-axis tracking plots:

  • Planned Trajectory (Blue): Target position requested by G-code.
  • Actual Feedback Position (Red): Encoder / motor feedback reported by controller.
  • Position Error (Green): Difference \(\Delta z(t) = z_{\text{actual}}(t) - z_{\text{planned}}(t)\).

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Performance Indicators
docs.text:
The telemetry panel displays:

  • Current Axis Positions: Live coordinates \((X, Y, Z, U, V, W)\).
  • Actual Speed / Velocity: Real-time motion speed in \(\text{mm/s}\).
  • Buffer State: Controller G-code command buffer fill level (prevents buffer underruns during high-frequency motion).
  • Trigger Event Counter: Total number of Geiger trigger pulses issued during the session.

docs.title: 3. Logging & Data Export
docs.text:
TRACE automatically records execution logs for motion quality assurance (QA):

  • Save Log File: Exports execution history to CSV format (motion_log_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.csv).
  • QA Metrics:
    • Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) across the entire trajectory: $\(\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left(z_{\text{actual}}(i) - z_{\text{planned}}(i)\right)^2}\)$
    • Max Peak Position Error.
    • Trigger Jitter: Timing variation between planned phase and actual electrical pulse.
